summary: Creates a recognisable rhythm across the student year, using functional milestones, student need, external and place-based anchors, and deliberately created King’s moments to convene the institution, coordinate activity and commission new opportunities where they add value.
detailSummary:
King’s will create a clearer and more recognisable rhythm around the moments when students most need connection, orientation, opportunity, recovery, reflection and celebration. The functional milestones of university life, including enrolment, assessment, progression, return to study and completion, will provide a spine for this work. These moments do not occur at the same time for every programme or student group, so the framework will recognise common types of moment while allowing for different academic calendars and patterns of study.

Around this spine, King’s will coordinate activity in response to student need, draw selectively on cultural, religious, civic and social moments with genuine convening power, and make use of place-based opportunities across all King’s campuses and their surrounding communities. It will also deliberately create recurring King’s moments where giving an internal milestone greater visibility, shared identity or sense of occasion would add value.

A shared student journey framework and coordinated planning rhythm will help faculties, services, KCLSU and student groups plan around student need rather than separate organisational timetables. King’s Edge will provide the orchestration layer: convening partners around common principles, connecting existing provision, coordinating activity and communications, and working with teams across the university to commission new opportunities where gaps or strategic opportunities emerge. This will be developed in close alignment with transition and student success work elsewhere in the portfolio, particularly Programme 3: Access and Success.
problemSolved: King’s beyond-course offer is rich but weakly orchestrated across the student journey, so opportunities can cluster when students have limited capacity, become less visible when they are more ready to engage, and compete for attention rather than forming a coherent rhythm.
whatChanges: King’s establishes a shared rhythm for opportunities and participation alongside the course, coordinating existing activity and commissioning new opportunities around student need, functional milestones and moments with genuine convening power.

caseForChange.problem:
The academic journey gives students a relatively clear sense of progression through teaching, assessment and key milestones. The wider experience of being a King’s student is less structured. Students encounter a rich ecology of communities, relationships and opportunities beyond their course, but its timing and visibility do not always match their changing needs or capacity to engage.

Activity can cluster around moments such as Welcome, then become less visible when students may have more space or motivation to participate. Those who do not connect early can struggle to find recognisable routes back in, missing opportunities to build community, belonging, a sense of mattering, and the relationships and social capital that enrich their experience and future prospects.

Faculties, services, KCLSU and student groups also plan through different cycles and can compete for attention at the same moments. Without a shared rhythm, strong individual activity can combine into an experience that feels fragmented, poorly timed and difficult to navigate.
caseForChange.opportunity:
King’s can create a shared rhythm for opportunities and participation alongside the course, using functional milestones such as enrolment, assessment, progression and completion as a flexible spine while recognising that different cohorts encounter them at different times. Around this, activity can be shaped by changing student need, external and place-based moments with genuine convening power, and deliberately created King’s moments that give important milestones greater visibility and shared meaning.

King’s Edge can provide the orchestration needed to make that rhythm real: convening faculties, services, KCLSU and student groups around common principles, connecting and coordinating existing activity, and commissioning new opportunities where gaps or strategic possibilities emerge. This creates repeated points of entry into the wider King’s community while preserving flexibility for different programmes, campuses and student groups.
caseForChange.whyNow:
Higher education is facing a wider crisis of engagement, within the course and beyond it. Students are also balancing study with greater levels of paid work, caring responsibilities and other pressures, making ease of navigation, clear invitation and good timing increasingly important. At the same time, the sector is recognising how strongly belonging, connection, social capital and seeing one’s own identity and cultural capital reflected in university life shape student experience and success.

King’s has committed to building the richness of learning and opportunity beyond the course. As that ecology grows, the value students can realise from it will depend increasingly on how well it is orchestrated. A shared rhythm can help turn a growing collection of opportunities into a coherent experience that students can actually find, enter and benefit from.
caseForChange.intendedChange:
Students experience a more coherent and recognisable rhythm of opportunities and participation alongside their course, with repeated chances to connect, take part, reset, reflect and celebrate at points that better match their needs and capacity to engage.

Faculties, services, KCLSU and student groups plan around a shared understanding of the student journey rather than separate organisational cycles. Existing activity is better coordinated, gaps are addressed through targeted commissioning, and key moments become more visible and meaningful across the year.

The result is a wider King’s experience that is easier to enter and re-enter, strengthens community, belonging and social capital, and helps students realise more of the value available to them through life at King’s.
